name: Prepared implementation repository
whatTheyReceive: One GitHub repository containing the standalone npm-workspaces structure, a working React 18 and Vite application, a working NestJS service, the initial shared TypeScript package, Docker Compose PostgreSQL, environment examples, root development commands, starter tests, CI, and the pull-request template.
usedFor: A single implementation base so students start with product features rather than assembling frontend, backend, database, workspace, and review infrastructure.
readyWhen: A clean clone installs, starts the frontend and backend, connects to PostgreSQL, runs migrations and starter tests, and passes the prepared CI workflow.

name: Approved Monabid components and brand assets
whatTheyReceive: An approved folder inside the implementation repository containing the Monabid logo, colors, typography, layout tokens, RTL-ready primitives, and the conversation, result, item, chart, estimate, auction-house, catalog, evidence, and upload components selected for this project.
usedFor: A consistent Monabid interface without requiring junior developers to recreate the design system or extract components themselves.
readyWhen: The package is imported by the starter application and its supplied components have fixture-backed examples for the relevant main, loading, empty, error, mobile, Hebrew, and English states.

name: Auction data and benchmark fixture pack
whatTheyReceive: Sanitized source-neutral auction-house, auction, lot, and sale-result fixtures; exact source lineage; the representative Bright Data sample and field decision; named buyer and seller benchmark scenarios; synthetic contact and photo evidence; and dated exchange-rate records used by the demonstrations.
usedFor: P1 ingestion, P2 search, Buyer results, Seller comparables and valuation, privacy tests, staff-dashboard examples, and deterministic acceptance journeys without customer or bidder data.
readyWhen: Fixture validation passes, every source-derived record is traceable, benchmark scenarios name their fixture IDs, and the pack covers sold, unsold, upcoming, missing-data, multiple-category, multiple-currency, supported-valuation, and refusal cases.

name: Selected OpenAI-compatible service access
whatTheyReceive: The approved provider base URL, model identifier, environment-variable names, secure credential handoff, known free-tier or usage limits, and the project-owner decision record. The project owner may use the awesome-freellm-apis directory to evaluate candidates.
usedFor: P4’s Week 1 provider explanation and Hebrew/English smoke test, followed by P4’s provider adapter, schema validation, deterministic fixture provider, retry, and fallback work with B2 and S1.
readyWhen: The selected endpoint is OpenAI-compatible, credentials are supplied outside the public repository, known limits are recorded, and P4 can run the limited Hebrew and English structured-output smoke test.

name: Prepared public deployment environments
whatTheyReceive: A Cloudflare Pages frontend project, Render backend service, Render PostgreSQL database, protected environment configuration, health checks, and one public fixture-backed application URL.
usedFor: Cross-team integration from Week 5 onward and the final public demonstration of all fourteen features.
readyWhen: The integrated fixture-mode application deploys successfully, secrets stay server-side, health checks pass, and synthetic buyer, seller, and staff journeys are reachable from the public URL.
